piece_type: DTC broadcast TV ads (2; athlete sponsorship 'The Journey Forward')

cases.cat: Omission of risk information (non-compliant reminder ad)
cases.heading: False or Misleading Risk Presentation
cases.claim: “brought to you by Emgality proud partner of Team USA” with “I do a whole bunch of different things to try to prevent migraine because for me the pain is really tough” (Ryan Murphy TV Ad) | “By the time I was in college, migraine had me hiding from light and sound, it was isolating” (Allysa Seely TV Ad)
cases.context: Ads reference indication so do not qualify as reminder ads under 21 CFR 202.1(e)(2); no risk information at all.
cases.rationale: Ads suggesting an indication must include major statement of side effects and contraindications.
cases.check: Rule: if a piece names the product and mentions the disease/use, it is not a reminder ad and must include risk information.

cases.heading: False or Misleading Risk Presentation
cases.claim: The TV ads fail to either provide adequate provision or a brief summary as required by 21 CFR 202.1(e)(1).
cases.rationale: Broadcast ads require adequate provision for dissemination of labeling or a brief summary.
cases.check: Rule: broadcast ads must include adequate provision elements (toll-free number, website, print ad reference, HCP referral) or a brief summary.

cases.cat: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
cases.heading: Omission of Material Facts
cases.claim: Ryan Murphy TV Ad suggests use for the preventive treatment of migraine but does not specify adults; Allysa Seely TV Ad suggests use for the treatment of migraine but does not specify preventive treatment of migraine in adults.
cases.rationale: Fails to communicate the full indication.
cases.check: Rule: indication statements must include the label's population (e.g., 'adults') and use type (e.g., 'preventive').

cases.cat: Failure to submit at time of initial dissemination (Form FDA 2253)
cases.heading: Failure to Submit Under Form FDA-2253
cases.claim: A copy of each TV ad was not submitted to OPDP under cover of Form FDA-2253 at the time of initial publication.
cases.check: Rule: confirm Form FDA 2253 submission at first use.
